artifact.category_tag: Nonlinear Schrödinger equation, growth of Sobolev norms
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether typical solutions of NLS exhibit unbounded growth of Sobolev norms or weak decay to zero is widely regarded as open. Partial results exist showing the existence of particular solutions with growing Sobolev norms (Bourgain, Kuksin, Colliander–Keel–Staffilani–Takaoka–Tao, Guardia–Kaloshin, Hani, Guardia–Hani–Haus–Maspero–Procesi, and many others), and unbounded growth has been established on irrational tori and other settings, but the genericity statement about typical initial data remains unresolved.

status_evidence.title: Growth of Sobolev norms in the cubic defocusing nonlinear Schrödinger equation
status_evidence.snippet: First lower bounds on the growth of Sobolev norms are due to Bourgain and Kuksin; constructing solutions with growing high Sobolev norms remains a central problem.
status_evidence.claim: The existence of unbounded Sobolev-norm trajectories for NLS on compact domains is a difficult, only partially resolved problem; the typical/generic version remains open.

status_evidence.title: Sobolev norm growths for Schrödinger equations
status_evidence.snippet: Project page summarizing partial results on growth of Sobolev norms for NLS, indicating that genericity of unbounded growth is not established.
status_evidence.claim: No published result establishes (a), (a'), (b), or (b') for typical initial data in H^m.
